Clinical Features
- Up to 20% of women with the infection may be asymptomatic
- If symptoms occur, they usually consist of vulval itching, soreness and a
non-offensive vaginal discharge which may be curdy
- Clinical examination:
- Vulval erythema (redness) or excoriations from scratching
- Vulval oedema
- Erosions and crusting on the adjacent intertriginous skin
- Although treatment of sexual partners is not recommended, it may be
considered for women who have recurrent infections
- A minority of male partners may have balanitis, which is characterized by
erythema of the glans penis or inflammation of the glans penis and foreskin
(balanoposthitis)
